header.title: Storage and Disks
header.description: Curated reference for storage inspection on Proxmox hosts: block devices, partitions, mounts, LVM volumes, Proxmox storage configuration, and a few VM disk operations (importdisk, qemu-img convert).

intro.title: Quick disk inventory
intro.body: lsblk shows block devices and partitions in a tree. Inspect persistent identifiers with ls -lh /dev/disk/by-id/: these normally remain stable across reboots and device reordering for the same disk. Replacing a disk or changing the way a controller exposes its identity can change its by-id path.

lvmTip.title: LVM short vs long commands
lvmTip.bodyRich: Both forms are available. pvs / vgs / lvs produce compact tables with one row per physical volume, volume group or logical volume respectively. pvdisplay / vgdisplay / lvdisplay provide more detailed multi-line output. The short forms are convenient for everyday checks.

smartInfo.title: SMART for SATA/SAS vs NVMe
smartInfo.bodyRich: SATA / SAS disks, including SSDs, can be inspected with smartctl from smartmontools (installed by default on Proxmox). Specify the device, for example /dev/sda or /dev/sdb. NVMe disks use a different native protocol. smartctl also supports them, while nvme from nvme-cli provides NVMe-specific controller, namespace and health queries. Install it with apt install nvme-cli if absent.

selfTestWarn.title: Self-tests run in the background
selfTestWarn.bodyRich: On supported drives, smartctl -t short /dev/<disk> and smartctl -t long /dev/<disk> start background tests and return immediately. Check progress with smartctl -a /dev/<disk> (look for "Self-test routine in progress") or wait and read smartctl -l selftest /dev/<disk>. Short tests commonly take about two minutes; long tests can take hours. The disk remains usable, but testing can reduce I/O performance.
